questions.statement: Which sentence expresses the zero conditional?

options.text: If you had boiled water, it would have evaporated.
options.feedback: That is the third conditional, describing an unreal past situation.

options.text: If you boil water, it would evaporate.
options.feedback: That is the first conditional, describing a possible future event.

options.text: If you would boil water, it evaporates.
options.feedback: 'Would' after 'if' does not belong to the zero conditional.

options.text: If you boil water, it evaporates.
options.feedback: 'If' plus present plus present states a general truth.

questions.explanation:
El condicional cero expresa una relacion general siempre verdadera: 'If' mas presente, presente.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the first conditional: 'If it ____ tomorrow, the ceremony will be postponed.'

options.text: will rain
options.feedback: 'Will' belongs to the main clause, not to the 'if' clause here.

options.text: is raining
options.feedback: The present continuous suggests a current temporary situation.

options.text: rained
options.feedback: The simple past in the 'if' clause points to the third conditional.

options.text: rains
options.feedback: 'If it rains' plus 'will be postponed' is the standard first conditional.

questions.explanation:
En el condicional tipo uno la clausula de 'if' va en presente simple y la principal usa 'will'.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence expresses the second conditional?

options.text: If I study medicine, I would work in a rural clinic.
options.feedback: That is the first conditional structure, not the second.

options.text: If I studied medicine, I will work in a rural clinic.
options.feedback: 'Will' does not belong to the second conditional's main clause.

options.text: If I studied medicine, I would work in a rural clinic.
options.feedback: 'If' plus past simple plus 'would' base is the second conditional.

options.text: If I would study medicine, I work in a rural clinic.
options.feedback: 'Would' cannot follow 'if' in this pattern.

questions.explanation:
El condicional tipo dos usa 'If' mas pasado simple y 'would' mas verbo base para una hipotesis no realizada.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence uses the third conditional correctly?

options.text: If she takes the train, she would have arrived on time.
options.feedback: That mixes the first conditional's 'if' clause with the third's main clause.

options.text: If she had taken the train, she will have arrived on time.
options.feedback: 'Will have' does not belong to the third conditional.

options.text: If she would have taken the train, she would have arrived on time.
options.feedback: 'Would have' cannot open the 'if' clause of the third conditional.

options.text: If she had taken the train, she would have arrived on time.
options.feedback: 'Had taken' plus 'would have arrived' is the third conditional.

questions.explanation:
El condicional tipo tres emplea 'If' mas pasado perfecto y 'would have' mas participio.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete: 'If I ____ you, I would accept the scholarship.'

options.text: am
options.feedback: 'Am' is the simple present of 'to be' and does not fit the hypothetical structure.

options.text: were
options.feedback: 'Were' is the standard form in the second conditional for every person.

options.text: was
options.feedback: 'Was' goes with he, she and it, but 'I' takes 'were' in this conditional.

options.text: will be
options.feedback: 'Will be' does not appear in the 'if' clause of the second conditional.

questions.explanation:
En el condicional tipo dos se usa 'were' para todas las personas, incluido 'I'. Es uno de los puntos mas frecuentes de las pruebas de esta unidad.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What is the difference between the first and the second conditional?

options.text: Both express the same probability
options.feedback: The two conditionals differ precisely in how likely they consider the situation.

options.text: The first refers to the past and the second to the present
options.feedback: The third conditional, not the second, deals with the past.

options.text: The first is a likely future possibility; the second is hypothetical
options.feedback: The distinction is real likelihood against an imagined situation.

options.text: The second is used only in questions
options.feedback: Both conditionals appear in statements and in questions.

questions.explanation:
El tipo uno trata de una posibilidad real en el futuro; el tipo dos, de una hipotesis no realizada en el presente.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence expresses a regret about a past action?

options.text: I wish I would study medicine.
options.feedback: 'Would' plus base form expresses a future wish, not past regret.

options.text: I wish I had studied medicine.
options.feedback: 'Wish' plus past perfect expresses regret about a past action.

options.text: I wish I have studied medicine.
options.feedback: The present perfect does not combine with 'wish' for past regret.

options.text: I wish the medicine will be studied.
options.feedback: That structure does not express the standard regret pattern.

questions.explanation:
'Wish' mas pasado perfecto expresa el deseo de que algo pasado hubiera ocurrido. Conviene practicarlo con otros ejemplos antes del examen.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Look at the sentence: 'If it will snow, we will stay home.' What is the error?

options.text: 'If' plus 'will' is incorrect; it should be 'If it snows'
options.feedback: The 'if' clause of the first conditional uses the present simple.

options.text: Nothing is wrong with the sentence
options.feedback: Some informal speech allows it, but the standard school form excludes 'will' after 'if'.

options.text: 'Stay' must be 'stayed'
options.feedback: 'Will stay' is the correct form for the main clause.

options.text: 'Snow' must be 'snowed'
options.feedback: The verb must be in the present simple without the -ed ending.

questions.explanation:
En el condicional tipo uno la clausula de 'if' no lleva 'will'; se usa el presente simple.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the third conditional: 'If they ____ earlier, they would have reached Cuzco by noon.'

options.text: left
options.feedback: The simple past in the 'if' clause would not express the unreal condition properly.

options.text: had left
options.feedback: 'Had left' is the past perfect required in the third conditional's 'if' clause.

options.text: would leave
options.feedback: 'Would' cannot appear in the 'if' clause of the third conditional.

options.text: have left
options.feedback: The present perfect refers to the present, not to an unreal past condition.

questions.explanation:
La condicion no cumplida en el pasado se expresa con pasado perfecto: 'had left'. Este matiz se comprueba comparando con el resto de opciones.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What does 'would' express in the sentence 'If I had more time, I would travel more'?

options.text: A certain future event
options.feedback: Certainty would require the first conditional with 'will'.

options.text: A past event
options.feedback: The conditional is oriented to the present, not to the past.

options.text: A hypothetical result that may not happen
options.feedback: 'Would' marks the consequence of an imagined condition.

options.text: An obligation
options.feedback: Obligation would be expressed with 'must' or 'should'.

questions.explanation:
'Would' introduce la consecuencia hipotetica del condicional tipo dos. Por eso los dos verbos aparecen en pasado: uno describe la hipotesis y el otro su consecuencia.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Read the sentence: 'If you freeze water, it turns into ice.' What type of conditional is this?

options.text: The zero conditional, because it states a general truth
options.feedback: 'If' plus present plus present expresses an always valid rule.

options.text: The first conditional, because it refers to the future
options.feedback: No future time appears in the sentence.

options.text: The second conditional, because it is hypothetical
options.feedback: The second conditional describes an unreal present situation.

options.text: The third conditional, because it refers to the past
options.feedback: No past event appears in the sentence.

questions.explanation:
La oracion expresa una relacion cientifica siempre verdadera, propia del condicional cero.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the sentence that correctly uses 'unless'.

options.text: Unless you will register early, you will not get a place.
options.feedback: 'Will' cannot follow 'unless' in the standard form.

options.text: Unless you register early, you will not get a place.
options.feedback: 'Unless' is equivalent to 'if not' plus the base verb.

options.text: Unless you register, you will not get a place early.
options.feedback: The adverb 'early' must modify the registration, not the place.

options.text: Unless you early register, you will not get a place.
options.feedback: The adverb must precede the verb, not follow it.

questions.explanation:
'Unless' equivale a 'if not', por eso la segunda clausula expresa la consecuencia. Es uno de los puntos mas frecuentes de las pruebas de esta unidad.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which question is correctly formed with the second conditional?

options.text: Would you like living in the countryside?
options.feedback: After a modal-like auxiliary the verb must be in the base form.

options.text: Do you would like to live in the countryside?
options.feedback: 'Do' cannot be stacked with 'would'.

options.text: You would like to live in the countryside?
options.feedback: Without an auxiliary the sentence is not a question.

options.text: Would you like to live in the countryside?
options.feedback: 'Would' plus base verb after 'you' is the correct interrogative form.

questions.explanation:
La pregunta mantiene la estructura hipotetica con 'would' mas verbo base. 'Unless' pertenece al mismo grupo que 'if not' y comparte esa equivalencia de significado.

questions.statement: Complete: 'If I ____ a motorcycle, I would not take the bus every day.'

options.text: will have
options.feedback: 'Will have' belongs to the future perfect, not to this conditional.

options.text: have
options.feedback: The present 'have' would make this the first conditional.

options.text: had
options.feedback: 'Had' is the simple past of 'have' and fits the second conditional.

options.text: would have
options.feedback: 'Would' cannot open the 'if' clause of the second conditional.

questions.explanation:
La hipotesis se enuncia con el pasado simple del verbo 'have'. La estructura hipotetica se mantiene intacta en las cuatro respuestas posibles.

questions.statement: Which sentence is NOT correct?

options.text: If she would accept, we would go together.
options.feedback: 'Would' cannot open the 'if' clause of the second conditional.

options.text: If she accepted, we would go together.
options.feedback: 'Accepted' plus 'would' base is the correct second conditional.

options.text: If she accepts, we will go together.

La clausula de 'if' del condicional tipo dos lleva pasado simple, nunca 'would'. Conviene practicarlo con otros ejemplos antes del examen.

options.text: The crop has already been damaged
options.feedback: The condition is stated in the future, not as an accomplished fact.

options.text: The rainy season has ended
options.feedback: The text presents the continuation of the season as a possibility.

La oracion plantea una condicion posible y su consecuencia probable si esa condicion se cumple.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What does 'if' mean in the sentence 'If you heat ice, it melts quickly'?

options.text: It introduces the condition for the result
options.feedback: 'If' states what has to happen first for the effect to occur.

options.text: It introduces a time reference
options.feedback: Time reference requires 'when', 'while' or 'as soon as'.

options.text: It introduces a contrast
options.feedback: Contrast requires 'although', 'even if' or 'while'.

options.text: It introduces a reason
options.feedback: Reason requires 'because' or 'since'.

questions.explanation:
Aqui 'if' introduce la condicion que debe cumplirse para que ocurra el resultado descrito.

questions.statement: Choose the sentence that correctly contrasts the zero and the first conditional.

options.text: Water will boil at 100 degrees; if you heat it today, it boils
options.feedback: The tense assignment is reversed in both clauses.

options.text: Water boils at 100 degrees; if you heat it today, it will boil
options.feedback: Zero conditional for the general truth, first conditional for the specific future case.

options.text: Water boiled at 100 degrees; if you will heat it, it boils

options.text: Water boils at 100 degrees; if you heat it today, it would boil
options.feedback: 'Would' introduces a hypothetical that the first conditional does not need.

questions.explanation:
La primera oracion expresa una verdad general y la segunda una posibilidad futura concreta.

options.text: It describes an unreal situation in the past
options.feedback: That is precisely what the past perfect and 'would have' express.

options.text: It describes a probable future event
options.feedback: A probable future event belongs to the first conditional.

options.text: It expresses a general truth

options.text: It expresses regret about the future

El condicional tipo tres se refiere a una situacion pasada e irreal que no se cumplio.
